anchor.quote: while the width falls by a factor $m$
anchor.note: The page uses m as the factor by which the width falls at each recursion level. The earlier pages bind m only to other objects (label space dimension, coefficient count, digit count), and none of them tells the reader that m is this factor.

gaps.term: precision p of order lg n
gaps.quote: The computed values keep $p$ bits after each rounding, the precision, which is of order $\lg n$.
gaps.note: The page asserts that the precision p is of order lg n but never says why the rounding precision must grow like lg n or how it is chosen.

gaps.quote: Undoing the digit scales leaves an error of a constant times $b\,2^{-3b/4}$ for the digit width $b$.
gaps.note: The error bound b 2^(-3b/4) is presented as the result of undoing the digit scales, but no calculation is shown and it is not marked as cited. The reader cannot check it, and the scaling is not explained.

gaps.quote: since the coefficient error is below $1/2$
gaps.note: The page never says how b is chosen relative to n, nor how the p-bit rounding error combines with the b 2^(-3b/4) term. So the claim that the total error is below 1/2 does not follow from what the page gives.
The page states that the stored volume V is Theta(n) without saying how the array size is set from the input length.

gaps.quote: each displayed power there is at most $1-2\kappa$ (cited)
gaps.note: The cited bound refers to a cost table and its displayed powers, but the page does not say what the table contains or which operations it charges, so the reader cannot tell what the bound covers.
The page combines the cited table bound with the cited log absorption into one total, but does not say how many terms there are or why combining them keeps the exponent at 1 - kappa.

gaps.quote: Each recursion level multiplies the cost by $s/W$
gaps.note: The page does not say why each recursion level multiplies the cost by s/W, and gives no link or argument for this factor.

gaps.quote: So the level costs form a geometric series with ratio $(s/W)m^{-\tau}<1$, dominated by its first term.
gaps.note: The page asserts that the ratio (s/W) m^(-tau) is below 1 without any inequality relating s, W, m and tau, and m is unbound. The geometric-series domination also needs the ratio to stay bounded away from 1, which is not shown.

The page uses slack without defining it and says its smallest value is 2^(-181), so kappa is half of it. The reader cannot tell what slack measures or why its smallest value is that, and the cited claim does not say.
